claims.text: Thermomechanical processing by warm working followed by annealing will create a bimodal grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The resulting bimodal grain structure will increase tensile ductility.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by at least approximately 30% relative to a 13.5% baseline.
The treatment will preserve a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The reported 13.5% strain for HfZrTiTa0.53 is uniform tensile elongation.
The proposed bimodal structure consists of fine equiaxed grains interspersed with coarser grains.
A bimodal grain structure will reduce localized stress concentrations during tensile loading.
A bimodal grain structure will promote non-localized plastic flow during tensile loading.
Fine-grained regions will enhance work hardening.
Fine-grained regions will delay crack nucleation.
Coarser grains will facilitate strain accommodation.
Coarser grains will improve uniform elongation.
The processed alloy will reach approximately 18% or greater uniform tensile elongation.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength within approximately 10% of 786 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain compressive strength within approximately 10% of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has demonstrated impact energy release in penetration tests.
The hypothesis is limited to room-temperature tension and compression below 10^-3 s^-1 and to standard ambient impact-test configurations.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis reclassifies the reported 13.5% terminal strain as uniform tensile elongation, whereas the query does not identify it as uniform elongation and presents it alongside compressive properties.

The hypothesis attributes demonstrated penetration-test energy release to HfZrTiTa0.53, while the query attributes the reported energetic penetration result to WFeNiMo fragments rather than to HfZrTiTa0.53.
